key_insight: HippoCamp introduces a user-centric benchmark that measures agents' ability to model individual user profiles and search device-scale, multimodal personal files for context-aware reasoning — shifting evaluation from generic tool use to real-world personal computing scenarios.
problem_solved: Existing agent benchmarks ignore the challenges of personal, device-scale file management and profile-aware retrieval; HippoCamp fills this gap by simulating real user environments and massive multimodal file stores to evaluate contextual agents.
method: Instantiate device-scale file systems built from real-world user profiles spanning diverse modalities (documents, images, code, logs, etc.).
Design multimodal retrieval and reasoning tasks that require profile modeling, context disambiguation, and long-range file search across the simulated file system.
Provide standardized scenarios and evaluation metrics to compare agents' context-aware file management, retrieval accuracy, and reasoning robustness.
impact: Enables practitioners to develop and benchmark agents that better understand individual users and operate effectively on personal computers, accelerating progress in personalized assistants, privacy-aware retrieval, and multimodal reasoning.
visual_elements: Schematic of a device-scale file system populated with multimodal files linked to a user profile (icons for docs, images, code, email).
Flow diagram: user query → profile-aware retrieval → multimodal reasoning → action/result.
Bar or radar chart comparing agent performance across modalities and task types (retrieval, reasoning, personalization).
Icon set highlighting key evaluation dimensions: scale, modality, privacy/context, and accuracy.
paper_title: HippoCamp: Benchmarking Contextual Agents on Personal Computers
paper_authors: Zhe Yang, Shulin Tian, Kairui Hu, Shuai Liu, Hoang-Nhat Nguyen
